title: Challenger receives takeover bid from TAL Daiichi Life
full_text:
Challenger has received a non-binding indicative takeover offer for the company.
In an ASX statement on 19 October, the firm said it has received a non-binding and conditional indicative offer from TAL Daiichi Life Australia Pty Limited.
TDA already owns a minority stake in the company which it acquired last year from MS&AD Insurance Group and is now seeking to acquire the remaining 79.5 per cent of ordinary shares in Challenger that it does not already own.
This would be via scheme of arrangement at $11.80 per share.
Challenger is one of Australia’s leading companies for retirement income and annuities products.
“Challenger notes that the offer represents a 17.7 per cent premium to Challenger’s one-month volume weighted average price (VWAP) of $10.03. The board of Challenger is considering the indicative offer,” it said in the statement.
“The proposal is subject to a number of conditions including satisfactory completion of due diligence, entry into a scheme implementation agreement on acceptable terms and approval from various regulatory bodies, and board recommendation.”
This is the second major M&A announcement for Challenger this year after it agreed in June to merge its multi-affiliate boutique business Fidante to Channel Capital. The Fidante division includes brands such as Kapstream, Impax Asset Management and Eiger Capital.
This scale of the combined business would position Channel Group as one of Australia’s largest investment platform and services businesses, supported by over 240 professionals across 11 global offices.
